title: Bills of Lading and Transport Documents: booking status at issue that lets originals go into circulation
content:
## Scope

At the issuance of a Bills of Lading and Transport Documents transport document, the status of the booking the document covers decides whether the cargo counts as on board, and so whether the tier's originals or none go into circulation at issue.

## Formal clause

1. At the moment of issue the cargo counts as on board when the booking the document covers has the status loaded, departed or closed.
2. A booking in the status gated in counts as on board only on a document type whose tier allows issuance once the cargo is gated in, before loading.
3. The booking read here is the booking record held by the documentation party of the document. A booking held by another customer is not read, and the cargo then counts as not on board.
4. When the booking is in any other status, the cargo does not count as on board, and no originals are put into circulation at issue.

## Matrix

| Booking record | Tier allows issuance on gate-in | Cargo counts as on board at issue |
|---|---|---|
| Documentation party's own, loaded / departed / closed | Either | Yes |
| Documentation party's own, gated in | Yes | Yes |
| Documentation party's own, gated in | No | No |
| Documentation party's own, any other status | Either | No |
| Held by another customer | Either | No (not read) |

## Hypothetical cases

- A document whose own booking shows loaded at the moment of issue: the cargo counts as on board.
- A document on a tier that does not allow issuance on gate-in, whose booking shows gated in: the cargo does not count as on board, and no originals go into circulation.

## Points of judgement

- **Wrong reading:** a booking of the consignee or of a related company showing departed will do. **Correct basis:** only the booking record held by the documentation party of the document is read.
- **Wrong reading:** the planned sailing date is enough. **Correct basis:** only the recorded booking status counts.
